vibe: AI supply-chain drama day: Anthropic beat the Pentagon in court and got hit by an infostealer campaign within the same 24 hours, while OpenAI and Musk's SpaceX had their ugliest public breakup yet.

cyber.title: TerminalFix Uses Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs to Deploy Reverse-Tunnel Backdoor
cyber.summary: Malware campaign spoofs Cloudflare's "verify you are human" page to trick people into pasting a script into Windows Run, silently installing a reverse-tunnel backdoor for persistent remote access. Same fake-CAPTCHA pattern behind several recent infostealer waves — worth a second look before clicking through any browser verification prompt.

cyber.title: Anthropic warns infostealer malware is hijacking Claude sessions to drain usage
cyber.summary: Anthropic says infostealer malware is now specifically hijacking active Claude sessions to drain usage/API credits rather than just harvesting passwords — a sign attackers are adapting classic infostealer tooling to target AI service accounts directly.

cyber.title: Critical unauthenticated access vuln in argocd-mcp (CVE-2026-82456)
cyber.summary: argocd-mcp binds its MCP HTTP transport to every network interface and accepts sessions without checking caller credentials whenever an ArgoCD API token is configured — anyone who can reach the listener can hijack the operator's token to create apps, trigger syncs, and modify Argo CD resources. Worth checking exposure on any MCP servers you're running.

ai.title: Anthropic Opens Research Preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS)
ai.summary: A shared spec letting AI agents safely operate physical devices — robots, lab equipment, industrial hardware — standardizing how a model talks to hardware instead of every integration being bespoke. Part of Anthropic's broader push into physical-world agents this week.

ai.title: Anthropic is cutting Claude Code's current weekly limits by 17%
ai.summary: Anthropic is cutting Claude Code's current weekly usage limits by 17%, no official reason given yet. Lands the same week Anthropic is pushing into compute-hungry areas like MHS and robotics — worth watching if it affects your day-to-day usage.

ai.title: OpenAI to end model access to Cursor after acquisition by Elon Musk's SpaceX
ai.summary: OpenAI is cutting off Cursor's access to its models after SpaceX completed its $60B acquisition of the coding startup, saying it "cannot be confident SpaceX will use our tech within our terms of service." Cutoff date is Nov 12; Cursor says OpenAI models are only ~5% of its traffic. Musk fired back on X calling Altman and Brockman "utterly untrustworthy."

ai.title: Judge blocks Pentagon blacklist of Anthropic as supply chain risk
ai.summary: A federal judge ruled the Pentagon's March blacklisting of Anthropic as a "supply chain risk" was unconstitutional retaliation for its public criticism of DoD's AI stance, not a genuine security finding. Talks had collapsed over autonomous-weapons safeguards; the ruling clears defense contractors to use Claude again.

ai.title: Google AI Introduces EnvHarness: adaptive training worlds for agents
ai.summary: A programmable layer that turns static agent training environments into ones that adapt as the agent learns, aimed at making RL training for agents less brittle. Research-preview stage.

ai.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
ai.summary: Two more music publishers file a copyright suit against Anthropic over training data, joining Universal Music in the ongoing legal pressure campaign — adds to Anthropic's stacked legal docket this week alongside the Pentagon case.

it.title: Running SQLite Apps on Docker and Kubernetes with Litestream
it.summary: Walkthrough of running SQLite-backed apps on Docker and Kubernetes with Litestream for continuous replication to object storage — a lightweight alternative to standing up a full Postgres/MySQL cluster for smaller containerized workloads.

videos.title: Why Does AI Need Access to the Web?
videos.verdict: SKIM — solid conceptual framing, light on hard specifics
videos.summary: Argues pre-trained LLMs are frozen knowledge snapshots, so agents acting on stale or hallucinated info fail confidently and fast (wrong prices, recommending a permanently-closed museum). Lays out 5 requirements for a trustworthy "web data infrastructure layer": grounded (citable), deep (full context, not snippets), fresh, correctly formatted (markdown/JSON not raw HTML), and fast enough to arrive before the answer is generated. Worth a skim if you build anything agent- or RAG-adjacent; skippable if you already think about grounding daily.
